findings.source_quote: οὐ τὸ πλεῖον λέγω, ἀλλὰ μόνον καὶ ὅλον τὸ τῆς ἁγνείας ἀναδέξασθαι
findings.english_quote: not, I say, something greater, but simply the whole of purity
findings.issue: “Something greater” obscures the quantitative contrast between the previously mentioned parts of purity and its whole. In this context τὸ πλεῖον is better represented as “the greater part” or “more,” rather than an unspecified greater thing. The draft does not discuss this choice or the construction μόνον καὶ ὅλον.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “not, I say, the greater part, but simply the whole of purity.” Add a source-quoted note retaining “more” as an alternative for τὸ πλεῖον, explaining why the preceding μέρη and following ὅλον favor the parts-versus-whole rendering, and identifying the adverbial reading of μόνον behind “simply.” The revised sentence requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: νοήσατε οὖν τὸν ἐκεῖ ὑμᾶς πεποιηκότα
findings.english_quote: So consider the one who made you act there
findings.issue: “Act” supplies an unexpressed complement to πεποιηκότα. A contextual causative reading referring back to their pursuit of purity is defensible, but it is not the only material reading of the supplied wording. The draft does not disclose this inference or preserve the more literal making/forming reading. This is an interpretive issue, not an established corruption requiring print verification.
findings.suggested_revision: If retaining “made you act there,” add a note quoting the Greek and explaining that “act” is inferred from the preceding description of pursuing purity, not restored from missing text. Preserve “the one who made you there,” understood as making or forming them as they were, as an alternative. Explain why the behavioral reading is preferred without identifying the unnamed agent. Review the revised text and note afresh.
